errors.english: Therefore, why would a momentary functional thing exclusively produce [a result], or why would the consequence be stated that it does not exclusively produce?
errors.why: This is a relative clause ('whatever consequence was stated: why does a momentary thing not produce by itself, why is it not alone?') whose predicate (it is to be understood as refuted) is on the next side; the English makes it a new question and inverts the first member.

note: Accurate rendering of a dense causal argument; only the side-final relative clause is mis-construed.
Faithful rendering of the pseudo-reason (asiddha) section, including the Digambara tree example.

errors.english: These phenomena are not without afflictions, nor are they possessed of afflictions.
errors.why: The sūtra says these dharmas are without affliction, they are not afflicted; the English negates the first member.

fix.find: These phenomena are not without afflictions, nor are they possessed of afflictions.
fix.replace: These phenomena are without afflictions; they are not possessed of afflictions.

errors.english: One should reverse the possibility of such a position.
errors.why: ji ltar srid pa means 'as applicable': the same fault is to be urged against simultaneous or later arising accordingly.

errors.english: no formation of the (skandhas) aggregates of existence
errors.why: In this list of afflictions phung por gyur pa means an accumulation/heap (of afflictions), not the five skandhas.

note: Generally readable, but a negation in the Akṣayamati quotation is reversed and two phrases are misread.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because number and possession are both
errors.why: ldan pa here is the Vaiśeṣika guṇa saṃyoga (conjunction): number and conjunction, both qualities, are impossible for the categories.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because number and possession are both
fix.replace: number and conjunction (saṃyoga) are also impossible for them, because number and conjunction are both

errors.english: Regarding the other position, the author states "Now..." and so forth.
errors.why: gzhan gyis marks the opponent as the speaker: 'The other says "Now..."'.

note: Sound rendering of the Vaiśeṣika critique; one Vaiśeṣika term and one speaker attribution need correcting.

errors.english: a collection of seeds and the seeds of the abodes of living beings have not been made "allowable"
errors.why: The list also includes sprouts that have broken through (khye'u kha 'thon pa), which is not rendered.

errors.english: even as little as a single blade of grass
errors.why: rtsa rgyud means a root-fibre/rootlet: 'even down to a root-fibre', not a blade of grass.

note: Good Vinaya rendering of the bhūtagrāma pāyantika; minor slips in the definition of the actual offence.
Faithful rendering of the sequence of faith and the guru's instruction.

errors.english: perfectly knows the causes and the conditions for change
errors.why: The phrase completes 'sems can rnams kyi rnam par dag par 'gyur ba' from the previous side: the causes and conditions for beings becoming purified, not 'for change'.

note: Accurate sūtra quotation on causes, conditions and the Tathāgata's absorptions; the opening phrase is misconstrued.

errors.english: Should not be despised in this world,
errors.why: The verse says the person should do what is not blamed in this world and brings happiness in the next; 'not blamed' qualifies the action, not the person.

fix.find: Should not be despised in this world,
fix.replace: Should do what is not blamed in this world

note: Good rendering of the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son examples; one verse is mis-construed.

errors.english: is for the purpose of reversing whatever one wishes to suppress
errors.why: This means it is to refute whoever holds the case to be blameworthy (na smad pa, a Vinaya term for incurring a penalty); 'suppress' misreads it.

note: A literal rendering of a difficult Vinaya commentary that stays opaque in places and needs a Vinaya specialist's pass on its euphemistic terms.

errors.english: for one who possesses a mind lacking the intent to deceive
errors.why: yid mi ches pa'i sems means a mind without confidence or conviction (in the power), not 'lacking the intent to deceive'.

note: Sound rendering of the toll-evasion rules; one phrase in the supernormal-power clause is misread.
